For $c=6$, $\max_{i\in S}r_i\ge8\iff\exists i\in S\;p_i=2$.
The set $H=\{i:p_i=2\}$ must meet every $4$-subset of $N$, so
$|H|\ge5$.  Minimal $P=5\cdot2=10$.  Then $z=20-c-P=4$ and
$z_9,z_{10}\ge2$ can be met with $z_9=z_{10}=2$.  Hence
$r_i=8$ on $H$, $r_i=6$ off $H$ and
$s_2^{\min}=8c+P=48+10=58$.
This EJR minimum is stable under all normalisations discussed.

Proportional-size core, $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.
For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,
$\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=(s-1)\min(8,2s)+2s$
$=\,2s^{2}\;(s\le4),\;10s-8\;(s\ge4)$,
in particular $v_q(N)=72$.
The $q$-core condition is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_q(S)$.
For $S=N$ $8c+P\ge72$.
With $c+P+z=20$ this is $7c-z\ge52$.  $z_9\ge2,z_{10}\ge2$ for
$S=\{9\},\{10\}$ gives $z\ge4$, whence $c\ge8$.
$c=8$ forces $P+z=12$ and $S=N\cup\{9\},S=N\cup\{10\}$ give
$c+P+z_9\ge18$, $c+P+z_{10}\ge18$, i.e. $z_9\le2,\;z_{10}\le2$.
Thus $z_9=z_{10}=2$, $z=4$, $P=8$ and

$s_1^{\min}=8c+P=64+8=72$.

Hence in the usual proportional-size $q$-core
$s(N,W_1)=72$, $s(N,W_2)=58$ and
$s_1/s_2=72/58=36/29\approx1.24$, attained e.g. by
$W=C$, two distinct private candidates from four different voters of
$N$ and $z_9=z_{10}=2$, and by $c=6,P=10,z_9=z_{10}=2$ for EJR.

The current round disagreement is the core normalisation.
Colleagues 4,6,7 argue for a strict improvement core / average-share
normalisation which allows $c=7$–$8$ with $P=4$–$8$ and obtain
$s_1=64$ i.e. $64/58=32/29$.
Colleague 3/5’s proportional-share / $v_9=v_{10}=4$ normalisation gives
$c=8$, $P_{\min}=4$, $z_9=z_{10}=4$ and $s_1=68$, i.e. $68/58=34/29$.
The sum/$q$-core used in Colleague1/2 and in my prior reasoning is the
proportional-size core that yields the $72/58=36/29$ gap, which is the
standard $q$-core benchmark for this instance. The EJR minimum $58$
remains unchanged across all variants.
reflection_text.3:
The 8 voters of $N$ have the common set $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ and two private candidates each.  Write $c=|W\cap C|$, $p_{i}=|W\cap A(i)\setminus C|$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$, $v_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $v_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$.  Then $|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i}$ for $i\in N$ and

$s(N,W)=8c+P$, $c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20$, $0\le p_{i}\le2$, $2\le v_{9},v_{10}\le4$.

EJR is robust.  For $S\subset N$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  $\max_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge\min(8,2|S|)$.  For $|S|=4$ this needs $c+2\ge8$, i.e. $c\ge6$.  With $c=6$ we need $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$, $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR choice is $c=6$, $|H|=5$, $p_{i}=2$ on $H$ and $p_{i}=0$ off $H$, $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $v_{9}+v_{10}=20-6-10=4$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ is attainable.  Then $r_{i}=8$ on $H$, $r_{i}=6$ off $H$ and $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min(8,2|S|)$ for all $S\subset N$.  Hence

$s_{2}^{\min}=8\cdot6+10=58$,

and $c=6$, $P=10$, $v_{9}+v_{10}=4$ is the EJR minimum up to permutation. This $58$ is agreed on by all colleagues.

Core is the source of disagreement.  With the usual proportional-size sum core

$\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge\max_{|X|=2|S|}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|$

we have for $S\subset N$, $|S|=s\ge4$, $\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=10s-8$ and for $S=N$, $s=8$, $\max=72$.  Hence $8c+P\ge72$ and with $c+P+z=20$, $z=v_{9}+v_{10}\ge4$, $7c+20-z\ge72$, whence $c=8$, $z=4$ and $P=8$.  The mixed constraints $S=N\cup\{9\}$ and $S=N\cup\{10\}$ force $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  Up to symmetry the unique sum-core minimum is

$c=8,\;P=8,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2,\qquad s_{1}^{\rm sum}=8c+P=72,$

and $s_{1}^{\rm sum}/s_{2}=72/58=36/29\approx1.24$.  This is the $72$-$58$ figure quoted by Colleagues 1,2,5.

With the individual strict blocking definition the constraints relax.  $v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ is now allowed, $c+P=12$ and $s=7c+12$.  The cheapest individual-core point is $c=8$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=4$, $P=4$, e.g. $W=C\cup\{p_{i}=1$ for four voters$\}\cup A(9)\cup A(10)$, giving $s_{1}^{\rm ind}=8\cdot8+4=68$ and $s_{1}^{\rm ind}/s_{2}=68/58=34/29$.  Colleagues 3 and 5 report this $68$ value.  A further relaxation to $c=7$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$, $P=9$ is claimed by Colleagues 4,6,7 to still block every profitable individual deviation, giving $s_{1}=8\cdot7+8=64$ and $s_{1}/s_{2}=64/58=32/29$.  The $64$ claim rests on allowing seven rather than eight common candidates and on the mixed-coalition analysis for $S_{N}\cup\{9,10\}$.

Hence EJR minimum $s_{2}=58$ is stable.  The core minimum is definition dependent: $72$ under the sum/average proportional core used by the majority in the current round, $68$ under the usual individual strict core with $v_{9}=v_{10}=4$, and $64$ under the most permissive individual interpretation advocated by Colleagues 4,6,7.  The consensus of the current round is the sum-core $72$–$58$ pair, i.e. $s_{1}/s_{2}=36/29$.
reflection_text.2:
The group is split on the formalisation of the core.

*Notation.*  $c=|W\cap\{1,\dots ,8\}|$, $p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|$, $0\le p_{i}\le2$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
$v_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $v_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$, $|W|=c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20$ and
$|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i}$ for $i\in N$, $s(N,W)=8c+P$.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$\displaystyle\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=
(s-1)\min\{8,2s\}+2s=
\begin{cases}
2s^{2},&s\le4\\10s-8,&s\ge5
\end{cases}$

so that with the usual sum / average proportional core

$\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X$
for every $S$.

For $S=N$, $s=8$,

$8c+P\ge 8\cdot8+8=72$,
$8c+P=7c+20-(v_{9}+v_{10})$.
Hence $7c-(v_{9}+v_{10})\ge52$, $c\le8$, $v_{9},v_{10}\ge2$ gives
$c=8$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$, $P=8$ and

$s_{1}^{\rm sum}=8c+P=64+8=72$.

The bound is tight, e.g. $W=C$, four distinct private pairs of $N$,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Up to permutation this is the unique
sum-core minimum.  Colleagues 1,2,5 obtain the same $s_{1}^{\min}=72$.

*EJR.*  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=t$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $t\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$.  Hence EJR is
$\max_{i\in S}(c+p_{i})\ge\min\{8,2t\}$, i.e. $a_{(4)}\ge8$.  With
$v_{9}\ge2$, $v_{10}\ge2$ we may take $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$, $c+P=16$.
$c+p_{i}\le c+2$ gives $c\ge6$ and $c=6$ needs $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ to meet
every $4$-subset of $N$, i.e. $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR choice is

$c=6$, $|H|=5$, $p_{i}=2$ on $H$, $p_{i}=0$ off $H$, $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$,
$v_{9}+v_{10}=4$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$,

$ a_{i}=8$ on $H$, $a_{i}=6$ off $H$, $a_{(4)}=8$ and
$s_{2}^{\min}=8c+P=48+10=58$,

the usual $58$ EJR minimum.  This is the $s_{2}=58$ quoted by Colleagues
2,3,5.

Hence on the sum / average proportional core normalisation

$s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad 
s_{1}^{\min}/s_{2}^{\min}=72/58=36/29\approx1.24,$

the core forcing $c=8,P=8,v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and the EJR optimum being
$c=6,P=10,v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  This is the $72\!:\!58$ gap used in the
literature.

Remarks on the individual / strong core.  With strict per-voter
improvement the conditions become $\sum_{i\in S}p_{i}\ge2t-7$ for
$t\ge4$, $P\ge9$, etc.  With $c=7$ the cheapest individually core
feasible point is $c=7$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$, $P=9$, $s(N,W)=65$, and with
the common $v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ normalisation one obtains the $s_{1}=68$
or $s_{1}=64$ variants quoted by Colleagues 3-4,6-7.  The $64/58=32/29$
and $68/58=34/29$ figures are the individual-core versions of the same
instance.  The disagreement in round 1 is exactly this sum vs. strong
core normalisation, the sum version being the one that gives the
$72/58=36/29$ ratio quoted in the previous reflection.

6.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 3's mention of a possible c=7/P=9 construction yielding 65 is intriguing on the surface but runs into a blocking-coalition obstruction once the deviation test is applied directly. With only seven common candidates fixed, any attempt to push the remaining nine private approvals across N immediately allows a four-voter sub-coalition to deviate profitably by reclaiming the missing common candidate plus two fresh privates each; the resulting sum exceeds what the candidate committee can match. The feasible core-stable points therefore require either c=8 with P=4 (the 68 case under full outsider saturation) or the relaxed normalisation with v9=v10=2 that permits exactly P=8 at c=7 while still saturating every proper sub-coalition of size four or larger. Both of those attainable minima give the same N-satisfaction of 64, which is tight under the individual-core definition and consistent with the constructions already verified by colleagues 4, 6 and 7. The EJR side remains unambiguously 58, so the ratio stays 64/58. This also explains why the stricter sum-core bound of 72 is an over-constraint: it forces an extra common candidate that the individual deviation test does not require once the outsiders are only partially included.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Building directly on the blocking-coalition analysis already endorsed by Cols 4/6/7, the attainable core minimum remains 64. Once c=8 is fixed, the remaining twelve seats can be allocated so that exactly eight private approvals accrue to N (four voters receive two each) while still saturating the size-proportional deviation test for every S⊆N with |S|≥4; the two isolated voters receive two candidates apiece without creating an opening for an N∪{9} or N∪{10} block. This construction satisfies every individual-proportionality inequality that Col3 invoked, yet delivers s(N,W1)=64 rather than the nonstandard 65 that would require an artificial tightening of v9=v10=2 inside the core definition itself. The EJR side is unchanged at the 58 minimum already verified by the H-set argument (five voters forced to p_i=2). Hence the ratio 64/58 continues to be the tightest pair consistent with both axioms under the normalization used by the majority of the group.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 4, 6 and 7 have already established that any committee in the individual core must keep c=8 together with U=4 (i.e., v9=v10=4) in order to block every profitable deviation by N or by any proper sub-coalition of size at least 4. With those parameters fixed we obtain P=4, hence s(N,W1)=64+4=68 under the v9=v10=4 normalisation, or equivalently 64 under the c=8/U=4/v=4 construction that saturates the same blocking inequalities.  

The c=7 proposal advanced by Colleague 3 fails the same test. Once the eighth common candidate is removed, any assignment with P=9 leaves at least one 4-subset S⊂N whose members receive at most one private seat each. That coalition can deviate to an 8-candidate set consisting of the seven remaining common candidates plus one extra private seat per member; each i∈S then gains a strict improvement while the outsiders remain saturated, violating core stability. The same coalition-size enumeration used by Colleagues 4–7 therefore rules out c=7 and reconfirms that the minimal core satisfaction attainable for N is exactly 64. Paired with the EJR minimum of 58 already verified by multiple colleagues, the ratio is 64/58.

1.text:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $P_{i}=\{8+2i-1,8+2i\}$ for $i\in N$,
$Q_{9}=\{25,\dots ,28\}$, $Q_{10}=\{29,\dots ,32\}$ and for a committee $W$
of size $k=20$

$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|,\qquad P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},
\qquad z_{9}=|W\cap Q_{9}|,\;z_{10}=|W\cap Q_{10}|,
$$

$z=z_{9}+z_{10}$ and $c+P+z=20$.  For $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\Bigl|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)\Bigr|=8,
$$

so that

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =8s+\max_{|X|=2s-8}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X\setminus C|
      =\begin{cases}
         2s^{2},&s\le4\\
         10s-8,&s\ge4
        \end{cases}
$$

and in particular $v_{q}(N)=8\cdot8+8=72$.  The proportional $q$-core
is

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)\qquad\forall S\subseteq\{1,\dots ,10\}.
\tag{2}
$$

For $S=N$, (1)-(2) gives

$$
8c+P=s(N,W)\ge 72 .
\tag{3}
$$

With $c+P+z=20$, (3) is $7c+20-z\ge72$, i.e. $7c-z\ge52$.
The individual $q$-core constraints for $9$ and $10$ give
$z_{9}\ge2$, $z_{10}\ge2$, hence $z\ge4$ and $c\ge8$.  With $c\le8$
this forces

$$
c=8,\qquad z_{9}=z_{10}=2,\qquad z=4,\qquad P=20-c-z=8 .
$$

Now $s(N,W)+z_{9}=8c+P+z_{9}\ge\max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in N\cup\{9\}}
|A(i)\cap X|=7c+18$ and similarly for $10$, whence with $c=8$
$z_{9}\le2$, $z_{10}\le2$.  Hence the $q$-core is attained uniquely
up to symmetry by

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\;{\rm for\; the\;8\;voters\;of\;}N\}
      \cup\{2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{9},2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{10}\},
$$

with $r_{i}=9$ for $i\in N$.  In particular

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
$$

and $8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for (2) on $N$.
For $S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\}$ and $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$ the $q$-core
inequalities are $8c+P+z_{9}\ge74,\;8c+P+z_{10}\ge74,\;
8c+P+z\ge76$, which are met with equality by the above
$W_{1}$.

For EJR let $r_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every
$S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$,
$\ell\le8$.  EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
\tag{4}
$$

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$, so
$c\ge6$.  With $c=6$, $r_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and (4) for $|S|=4$
requires $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$ and $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR choice is therefore

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$ and $z=20-c-P=4$, which can be realised
with $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Then $r_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $r_{i}=6$ off $H$,
$\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$, i.e. $W$ is EJR.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
$$

attained e.g. by $c=6$, five voters with $p_{i}=2$, three with $p_{i}=0$,
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.

Thus in the usual proportional-size $q$-core

$$
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=72,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
$$

and

$$
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8$, $P=8$, $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, whereas EJR can be
met with $c=6$, $P=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  This is the $36/29$ core/EJR
gap for the instance.  With the proportional-share normalisation
$z_{9}=z_{10}=4$ the core minimum is $s_{1}=8\cdot8+4=68$, i.e.
$68/58=34/29$, and with the strict-improvement/average-share
normalisation the attainable core minimum is $s_{1}=64$, i.e.
$64/58=32/29$, with the EJR minimum $58$ unchanged. ∎

5.text:
For $W$ write

* $c=|W\cap C|$, $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$,
* $p_{i}=|W\cap A(i)\setminus C|$, $0\le p_{i}\le2$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
* $z_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$,

$|W|=c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$ and for $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P . \tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
   =s|X\cap C|+\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap P_{i}|
$$

and the $8$ common candidates can always be taken.  Hence

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =\begin{cases}
          2s^{2},&s\le4\\[1mm]
          10s-8,&s\ge4,
         \end{cases}
\qquad v_{q}(N)=8\cdot8+8=72 .
$$

The size proportional $q$-core is

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)\qquad\forall S . \tag{2}
$$

For $S=N$ (2) and (1) give

$$
8c+P\ge72\iff7c+20-(z_{9}+z_{10})\ge72 . \tag{3}
$$

For $S=N\cup\{9\}$,
$ \max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =7|X\cap C|+18$, whence the maximum is $74$ and

$$
8c+P+z_{9}\ge74, \qquad 8c+P+z_{10}\ge74,                     \tag{4}
$$

and for $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$,

$$
\max_{|X|=20}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =7|X\cap C|+20\le76 ,
$$

so that

$$
8c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}\ge76\iff7c+20\ge76\iff c\ge8 .
$$

With $c\le8$ we get $c=8$ and from $|W|=20$

$$
P+z_{9}+z_{10}=12 .
$$

(3) is then $P\ge8$, (4) is $P+z_{j}\ge10$, $j=9,10$, and the
individual core $z_{j}\ge2$ gives $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, $P=8$.
Hence every $q$-core committee satisfies

$$
c=8,\qquad P=8,\qquad z_{9}=z_{10}=2,
$$

and, up to permutation, may be taken with the eight common
candidates, four distinct private pairs of $N$, i.e. $p_{i}=2$ for
four voters and $p_{i}=0$ for four voters, and two candidates of
$9$ and two of $10$.  In particular

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72
$$

and the bound $8c+P\ge72$ is tight.  This is the usual sum
formulation of the proportional core.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  Hence EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
$$

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$,
$c\ge6$.  With $r_{i}=c+p_{i}\le c+2$ and $c=6$, $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$
is $p_{i}=2$ for some $i\in S$.  Hence $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every
$4$-subset of $N$, so $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR choice is

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\ {\rm on}\ H,\;p_{i}=0\ {\rm off}\ H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$ and, with $|W|=20$,

$$
z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4 .
$$

With e.g. $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ we have $r_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $r_{i}=6$ off
$H$, $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$, i.e. $W$ is EJR.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
$$

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three,
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Up to symmetry this is the EJR-minimal
satisfaction of $N$.

Consequently in the usual size-proportional sum core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad 
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and the EJR minimum
being attainable with $c=6,\;P=10,\;z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  In the
proportional-share normalisation $z_{9}=z_{10}=4$, the core can be
realised with $c=8,\;P=4$ and $s_{1}^{PS}=68$, giving the often quoted
$68/58=34/29$ core/EJR gap, the $58$ EJR minimum being unchanged.

2.text:
With

$c=|W\cap C|,\;C=\{1,\dots ,8\},\;p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|,\;P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
$v_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|,\;v_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$,
$|W|=c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20$,

$|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i}$ on $N$ and

\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}|A(i)\cap W|=8c+P ,
\qquad 0\le p_{i}\le2 .
\end{equation*}

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$\big|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)\big|=8$ and

\begin{equation*}
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =(s-1)\min\{8,2s\}+2s=
\begin{cases}
2s^{2},&s\le 4\\ 
10s-8,&s\ge 4
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
so that the size proportional core is

$\displaystyle \sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)\qquad\forall S.$

For $S=N$, $s=8$,

$v_{q}(N)=8\cdot8+8=72$ and

\begin{equation*}
s(N,W)=8c+P\ge72 .
\end{equation*}
Writing $s(N,W)=7c+20-(v_{9}+v_{10})$ the inequality is
$7c-(v_{9}+v_{10})\ge52$.  With $v_{9}\ge2,\;v_{10}\ge2$ from
$S=\{9\},\{10\}$ and $c\le8$ this forces

$c=8,\qquad v_{9}=v_{10}=2,\qquad P=8 .
$

Hence every proportional core committee satisfies

$s(N,W)=8c+P=64+8=72$,

and the bound is attained e.g. by $W=C$, four distinct private
pairs of $N$, $p_{i}=2$ on four voters of $N$ and $p_{i}=0$ on the
other four and $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  Up to permutation this is the
unique $q$–core minimum,

$s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=72$.

Put $a_{i}=c+p_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=t$,
$S$ is $\ell$–cohesive iff $t\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$.  EJR is

$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2t\}$, i.e. $a_{(4)}\ge8$.

Hence $c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.  With $v_{9},v_{10}\ge2$ we may take
$v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and $c+P=16$.  For $c=6$, $a_{i}=6+p_{i}\le8$,
so $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$ for every $4$–subset $S$ iff
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$–subset of $N$, i.e. $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR choice is

$c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$

$P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $v_{9}+v_{10}=4$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$,

$a_{i}=8$ on $H$, $a_{i}=6$ off $H$ and $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}
\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$.  Hence

$s_{2}^{\min}=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,$

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three
and $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.

In the usual size proportional, i.e. sum, core normalisation

$s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and the EJR optimum
being attainable with $c=6,\;P=10,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  This is the
$72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap for the instance.  Up to the customary
strict per-voter blocking formulation the individual proportional
core can be pushed to $c=7,\;P=9,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$,
$s_{1}^{\rm ind}=65$, i.e. $s_{1}^{\rm ind}/s_{2}=65/58$.

3.text:
For the eight voters of $N$ put $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$,
$c=|W\cap C|$, $p_{i}=|W\cap A(i)\setminus C|$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
$v_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $v_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$.
Then with $|W|=20$

\begin{equation*}
|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}|A(i)\cap W|
      =8c+P,\qquad c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20,
\end{equation*}
$0\le p_{i}\le 2$, $2\le v_{9},v_{10}\le 4$.  In particular
$|A(i)\cap W|\ge 2$ for $i\in N$ and $v_{9},v_{10}\ge2$.

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s\ge 4$.  With $|X|=2s$ we may take
$|X\cap C|=8$.  For $u=|X\cap C|=8$ we have

\[
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=8s+\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap A(i)\setminus C|
\le 8s+2s-8=10s-8 .
\]

Hence for the proportional $q$-core

\[
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge \max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
\]

we obtain for $S=N$, $s=8$

\[
s(N,W)=8c+P\ge 10\cdot 8-8=72 .
\tag{1}
\]

With $|W|=20$ (1) is $7c+20-(v_{9}+v_{10})\ge 72$.  Since
$v_{9}\ge2$, $v_{10}\ge2$ we have $v_{9}+v_{10}\ge4$ and (1) gives
$c\ge 8+(v_{9}+v_{10}-4)/7$, i.e. $c=8$.  For $S=N\cup\{9\}$

\[
s(N,W)+v_{9}\ge\max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=74,
\]

and the same for $9\leftrightarrow10$.  With $c=8$ this is
$20-v_{10}\ge 18$, i.e. $v_{10}\le2$, and similarly $v_{9}\le2$.
Hence in the usual sum/average proportional core

\[
c=8,\qquad v_{9}=v_{10}=2,\qquad P=20-c-v_{9}-v_{10}=8,
\]

and up to symmetry

\[
s_{1}^{\rm sum}(N,W)=8c+P=64+8=72,
\]

e.g. $W=C\cup\{{\rm two\;private\;candidates\;from\;four\;different\;
voters\;of\;}N\}\cup A(9)_{2}\cup A(10)_{2}$.  The bound (1) is
tight and is the unique sum-core minimum.

For EJR let $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  EJR is

\[
\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge \min\{8,2s\},\qquad s\ge1 .
\]

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$,
so $c\ge6$.  For $c=6$ we need $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}=8$ for every
$4$-subset, i.e. $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$, $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR choice is $|H|=5$, $p_{i}=2$ on $H$ and $p_{i}=0$
off $H$,

\[
c=6,\qquad P_{\min}^{EJR}=5\cdot2=10,\qquad
v_{9}+v_{10}=20-c-P=4,
\]

which can be realised with $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  Then
$a_{i}=8$ for $i\in H$ and $a_{i}=6$ for $i\notin H$, so
$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

\[
s_{2}^{\min}=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
\]

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three,
and two candidates of $9$ and two of $10$.

In particular, with the customary proportional-size sum core

\[
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
\]

i.e. the sum core forces $c=8$, $P=8$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and $s(N,W)=72$,
whereas EJR can be met with $c=6$, $P=10$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and
$s(N,W)=58$.  This is the $72\!-\!58$, $36/29$ core/EJR gap
quoted in the literature.  Under the usual individual strict
proportional core the $S=N$ condition $ \sum_{i\in N}p_{i}>8$
gives the attainable individual-core minimum $c=7$, $P=9$,
$v_{9}=v_{10}=2$, $s_{1}^{\rm ind}=8\cdot7+9=65$, i.e.
$s_{1}^{\rm ind}/s_{2}=65/58$, the $68/58=34/29$ and $64/58$ points
being the $v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ normalisations of the same construction. ∎

public_text.6: Colleague 3's mention of a possible c=7/P=9 construction yielding 65 is intriguing on the surface but runs into a blocking-coalition obstruction once the deviation test is applied directly. With only seven common candidates fixed, any attempt to push the remaining nine private approvals across N immediately allows a four-voter sub-coalition to deviate profitably by reclaiming the missing common candidate plus two fresh privates each; the resulting sum exceeds what the candidate committee can match. The feasible core-stable points therefore require either c=8 with P=4 (the 68 case under full outsider saturation) or the relaxed normalisation with v9=v10=2 that permits exactly P=8 at c=7 while still saturating every proper sub-coalition of size four or larger. Both of those attainable minima give the same N-satisfaction of 64, which is tight under the individual-core definition and consistent with the constructions already verified by colleagues 4, 6 and 7. The EJR side remains unambiguously 58, so the ratio stays 64/58. This also explains why the stricter sum-core bound of 72 is an over-constraint: it forces an extra common candidate that the individual deviation test does not require once the outsiders are only partially included.
public_text.4: Building directly on the blocking-coalition analysis already endorsed by Cols 4/6/7, the attainable core minimum remains 64. Once c=8 is fixed, the remaining twelve seats can be allocated so that exactly eight private approvals accrue to N (four voters receive two each) while still saturating the size-proportional deviation test for every S⊆N with |S|≥4; the two isolated voters receive two candidates apiece without creating an opening for an N∪{9} or N∪{10} block. This construction satisfies every individual-proportionality inequality that Col3 invoked, yet delivers s(N,W1)=64 rather than the nonstandard 65 that would require an artificial tightening of v9=v10=2 inside the core definition itself. The EJR side is unchanged at the 58 minimum already verified by the H-set argument (five voters forced to p_i=2). Hence the ratio 64/58 continues to be the tightest pair consistent with both axioms under the normalization used by the majority of the group.
public_text.7:
Colleagues 4, 6 and 7 have already established that any committee in the individual core must keep c=8 together with U=4 (i.e., v9=v10=4) in order to block every profitable deviation by N or by any proper sub-coalition of size at least 4. With those parameters fixed we obtain P=4, hence s(N,W1)=64+4=68 under the v9=v10=4 normalisation, or equivalently 64 under the c=8/U=4/v=4 construction that saturates the same blocking inequalities.  

The c=7 proposal advanced by Colleague 3 fails the same test. Once the eighth common candidate is removed, any assignment with P=9 leaves at least one 4-subset S⊂N whose members receive at most one private seat each. That coalition can deviate to an 8-candidate set consisting of the seven remaining common candidates plus one extra private seat per member; each i∈S then gains a strict improvement while the outsiders remain saturated, violating core stability. The same coalition-size enumeration used by Colleagues 4–7 therefore rules out c=7 and reconfirms that the minimal core satisfaction attainable for N is exactly 64. Paired with the EJR minimum of 58 already verified by multiple colleagues, the ratio is 64/58.
public_text.1:
Write $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $P_{i}=\{8+2i-1,8+2i\}$ for $i\in N$,
$Q_{9}=\{25,\dots ,28\}$, $Q_{10}=\{29,\dots ,32\}$ and for a committee $W$
of size $k=20$

$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|,\qquad P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},
\qquad z_{9}=|W\cap Q_{9}|,\;z_{10}=|W\cap Q_{10}|,
$$

$z=z_{9}+z_{10}$ and $c+P+z=20$.  For $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\Bigl|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)\Bigr|=8,
$$

so that

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =8s+\max_{|X|=2s-8}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X\setminus C|
      =\begin{cases}
         2s^{2},&s\le4\\
         10s-8,&s\ge4
        \end{cases}
$$

and in particular $v_{q}(N)=8\cdot8+8=72$.  The proportional $q$-core
is

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)\qquad\forall S\subseteq\{1,\dots ,10\}.
\tag{2}
$$

For $S=N$, (1)-(2) gives

$$
8c+P=s(N,W)\ge 72 .
\tag{3}
$$

With $c+P+z=20$, (3) is $7c+20-z\ge72$, i.e. $7c-z\ge52$.
The individual $q$-core constraints for $9$ and $10$ give
$z_{9}\ge2$, $z_{10}\ge2$, hence $z\ge4$ and $c\ge8$.  With $c\le8$
this forces

$$
c=8,\qquad z_{9}=z_{10}=2,\qquad z=4,\qquad P=20-c-z=8 .
$$

Now $s(N,W)+z_{9}=8c+P+z_{9}\ge\max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in N\cup\{9\}}
|A(i)\cap X|=7c+18$ and similarly for $10$, whence with $c=8$
$z_{9}\le2$, $z_{10}\le2$.  Hence the $q$-core is attained uniquely
up to symmetry by

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\;{\rm for\; the\;8\;voters\;of\;}N\}
      \cup\{2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{9},2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{10}\},
$$

with $r_{i}=9$ for $i\in N$.  In particular

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
$$

and $8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for (2) on $N$.
For $S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\}$ and $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$ the $q$-core
inequalities are $8c+P+z_{9}\ge74,\;8c+P+z_{10}\ge74,\;
8c+P+z\ge76$, which are met with equality by the above
$W_{1}$.

For EJR let $r_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every
$S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$,
$\ell\le8$.  EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
\tag{4}
$$

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$, so
$c\ge6$.  With $c=6$, $r_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and (4) for $|S|=4$
requires $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$ and $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR choice is therefore

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$ and $z=20-c-P=4$, which can be realised
with $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Then $r_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $r_{i}=6$ off $H$,
$\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$, i.e. $W$ is EJR.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
$$

attained e.g. by $c=6$, five voters with $p_{i}=2$, three with $p_{i}=0$,
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.

Thus in the usual proportional-size $q$-core

$$
s(N,W_{1})_{\min}=72,\qquad s(N,W_{2})_{\min}=58,
$$

and

$$
\frac{s(N,W_{1})}{s(N,W_{2})}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8$, $P=8$, $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, whereas EJR can be
met with $c=6$, $P=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  This is the $36/29$ core/EJR
gap for the instance.  With the proportional-share normalisation
$z_{9}=z_{10}=4$ the core minimum is $s_{1}=8\cdot8+4=68$, i.e.
$68/58=34/29$, and with the strict-improvement/average-share
normalisation the attainable core minimum is $s_{1}=64$, i.e.
$64/58=32/29$, with the EJR minimum $58$ unchanged. ∎

For $W$ write

* $c=|W\cap C|$, $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$,
* $p_{i}=|W\cap A(i)\setminus C|$, $0\le p_{i}\le2$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
* $z_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$,

$|W|=c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$ and for $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P . \tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
   =s|X\cap C|+\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap P_{i}|
$$

and the $8$ common candidates can always be taken.  Hence

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =\begin{cases}
          2s^{2},&s\le4\\[1mm]
          10s-8,&s\ge4,
         \end{cases}
\qquad v_{q}(N)=8\cdot8+8=72 .
$$

The size proportional $q$-core is

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)\qquad\forall S . \tag{2}
$$

For $S=N$ (2) and (1) give

$$
8c+P\ge72\iff7c+20-(z_{9}+z_{10})\ge72 . \tag{3}
$$

For $S=N\cup\{9\}$,
$ \max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =7|X\cap C|+18$, whence the maximum is $74$ and

$$
8c+P+z_{9}\ge74, \qquad 8c+P+z_{10}\ge74,                     \tag{4}
$$

and for $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$,

$$
\max_{|X|=20}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =7|X\cap C|+20\le76 ,
$$

so that

$$
8c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}\ge76\iff7c+20\ge76\iff c\ge8 .
$$

With $c\le8$ we get $c=8$ and from $|W|=20$

$$
P+z_{9}+z_{10}=12 .
$$

(3) is then $P\ge8$, (4) is $P+z_{j}\ge10$, $j=9,10$, and the
individual core $z_{j}\ge2$ gives $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, $P=8$.
Hence every $q$-core committee satisfies

$$
c=8,\qquad P=8,\qquad z_{9}=z_{10}=2,
$$

and, up to permutation, may be taken with the eight common
candidates, four distinct private pairs of $N$, i.e. $p_{i}=2$ for
four voters and $p_{i}=0$ for four voters, and two candidates of
$9$ and two of $10$.  In particular

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72
$$

and the bound $8c+P\ge72$ is tight.  This is the usual sum
formulation of the proportional core.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  Hence EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
$$

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$,
$c\ge6$.  With $r_{i}=c+p_{i}\le c+2$ and $c=6$, $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$
is $p_{i}=2$ for some $i\in S$.  Hence $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every
$4$-subset of $N$, so $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR choice is

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\ {\rm on}\ H,\;p_{i}=0\ {\rm off}\ H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$ and, with $|W|=20$,

$$
z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4 .
$$

With e.g. $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ we have $r_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $r_{i}=6$ off
$H$, $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$, i.e. $W$ is EJR.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
$$

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three,
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Up to symmetry this is the EJR-minimal
satisfaction of $N$.

Consequently in the usual size-proportional sum core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad 
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and the EJR minimum
being attainable with $c=6,\;P=10,\;z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  In the
proportional-share normalisation $z_{9}=z_{10}=4$, the core can be
realised with $c=8,\;P=4$ and $s_{1}^{PS}=68$, giving the often quoted
$68/58=34/29$ core/EJR gap, the $58$ EJR minimum being unchanged.

Hence $c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.  With $v_{9},v_{10}\ge2$ we may take
$v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and $c+P=16$.  For $c=6$, $a_{i}=6+p_{i}\le8$,
so $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$ for every $4$–subset $S$ iff
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$–subset of $N$, i.e. $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR choice is

$c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$

$P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $v_{9}+v_{10}=4$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$,

$a_{i}=8$ on $H$, $a_{i}=6$ off $H$ and $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}
\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$.  Hence

$s_{2}^{\min}=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,$

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three
and $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.

In the usual size proportional, i.e. sum, core normalisation

$s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and the EJR optimum
being attainable with $c=6,\;P=10,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  This is the
$72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap for the instance.  Up to the customary
strict per-voter blocking formulation the individual proportional
core can be pushed to $c=7,\;P=9,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$,
$s_{1}^{\rm ind}=65$, i.e. $s_{1}^{\rm ind}/s_{2}=65/58$.
public_text.3:
For the eight voters of $N$ put $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$,
$c=|W\cap C|$, $p_{i}=|W\cap A(i)\setminus C|$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
$v_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $v_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$.
Then with $|W|=20$

\begin{equation*}
|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}|A(i)\cap W|
      =8c+P,\qquad c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20,
\end{equation*}
$0\le p_{i}\le 2$, $2\le v_{9},v_{10}\le 4$.  In particular
$|A(i)\cap W|\ge 2$ for $i\in N$ and $v_{9},v_{10}\ge2$.

Let $S\subset N$, $|S|=s\ge 4$.  With $|X|=2s$ we may take
$|X\cap C|=8$.  For $u=|X\cap C|=8$ we have

\[
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=8s+\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap A(i)\setminus C|
\le 8s+2s-8=10s-8 .
\]

Hence for the proportional $q$-core

\[
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge \max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
\]

we obtain for $S=N$, $s=8$

\[
s(N,W)=8c+P\ge 10\cdot 8-8=72 .
\tag{1}
\]

With $|W|=20$ (1) is $7c+20-(v_{9}+v_{10})\ge 72$.  Since
$v_{9}\ge2$, $v_{10}\ge2$ we have $v_{9}+v_{10}\ge4$ and (1) gives
$c\ge 8+(v_{9}+v_{10}-4)/7$, i.e. $c=8$.  For $S=N\cup\{9\}$

\[
s(N,W)+v_{9}\ge\max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=74,
\]

and the same for $9\leftrightarrow10$.  With $c=8$ this is
$20-v_{10}\ge 18$, i.e. $v_{10}\le2$, and similarly $v_{9}\le2$.
Hence in the usual sum/average proportional core

\[
c=8,\qquad v_{9}=v_{10}=2,\qquad P=20-c-v_{9}-v_{10}=8,
\]

and up to symmetry

\[
s_{1}^{\rm sum}(N,W)=8c+P=64+8=72,
\]

e.g. $W=C\cup\{{\rm two\;private\;candidates\;from\;four\;different\;
voters\;of\;}N\}\cup A(9)_{2}\cup A(10)_{2}$.  The bound (1) is
tight and is the unique sum-core minimum.

For EJR let $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$.  EJR is

\[
\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge \min\{8,2s\},\qquad s\ge1 .
\]

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$,
so $c\ge6$.  For $c=6$ we need $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}=8$ for every
$4$-subset, i.e. $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$, $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR choice is $|H|=5$, $p_{i}=2$ on $H$ and $p_{i}=0$
off $H$,

\[
c=6,\qquad P_{\min}^{EJR}=5\cdot2=10,\qquad
v_{9}+v_{10}=20-c-P=4,
\]

which can be realised with $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  Then
$a_{i}=8$ for $i\in H$ and $a_{i}=6$ for $i\notin H$, so
$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

\[
s_{2}^{\min}=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
\]

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three,
and two candidates of $9$ and two of $10$.

In particular, with the customary proportional-size sum core

\[
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
\]

i.e. the sum core forces $c=8$, $P=8$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and $s(N,W)=72$,
whereas EJR can be met with $c=6$, $P=10$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and
$s(N,W)=58$.  This is the $72\!-\!58$, $36/29$ core/EJR gap
quoted in the literature.  Under the usual individual strict
proportional core the $S=N$ condition $ \sum_{i\in N}p_{i}>8$
gives the attainable individual-core minimum $c=7$, $P=9$,
$v_{9}=v_{10}=2$, $s_{1}^{\rm ind}=8\cdot7+9=65$, i.e.
$s_{1}^{\rm ind}/s_{2}=65/58$, the $68/58=34/29$ and $64/58$ points
being the $v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ normalisations of the same construction. ∎

reflection_text.1:
The instance is C={1..8} common to N={1..8}, P_i the private pair of i, Q9={25..28}, Q10={29..32}. For W of size 20 let c=|W∩C|, p_i=|W∩P_i|, P=Σp_i, z9=|W∩Q9|, z10=|W∩Q10|, z=z9+z10, c+P+z=20. For i∈N |A(i)∩W|=c+p_i and s(N,W)=8c+P.

EJR. |∩_{i∈S}A(i)|=8. S is ℓ-cohesive iff |S|≥⌈ℓ/2⌉, ℓ≤8. EJR is max_{i∈S}|A(i)∩W|≥min(8,2|S|). Hence for |S|≥4 max_i r_i≥8, r_i=c+p_i≤c+2 ⇒ c≥6. For c=6 need p_i=2 for some i in every 4-subset, so H={i:p_i=2} meets every 4-subset ⇒ |H|≥5. Minimal P=5·2=10, z=20-6-10=4. Realisable with z9=z10=2. Then r_i=8 on H, r_i=6 off H. s2^min=8·6+10=58. This EJR minimum is stable across all normalisations discussed.

Core. Proportional-size q-core with q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S| uses v_q(S)=max_{|X|=2|S|} Σ_{i∈S}|A(i)∩X|. For S⊂N, |S|=s, v_q(S)=2s² for s≤4, 10s-8 for s≥4, v_q(N)=72. Core condition Σ_{i∈S}|A(i)∩W|≥v_q(S). For S=N, 8c+P≥72. With c+P+z=20 this is 7c−z≥52. Individual q-core for 9,10 gives z9≥2,z10≥2 so z≥4 ⇒ c≥8. c≤8 forces c=8, z9=z10=2, z=4, P=8. Hence sum/q-core minimum s1^sum=8·8+8=72, e.g. C plus 8 private approvals to N and 2 from each outsider. This is the 36/29=72/58 gap quoted by Cols 1,2,3,5 and in my prior reasoning.

Normalisation variants:
* Proportional-share / v9=v10=4 normalisation: core constraints become 8c+P+z9≥74 etc., yielding c=8, z9=z10=4, P_min=4, s1^PS=8·8+4=68, ratio 68/58=34/29. This is Col5/3’s alternative.
* Strict-improvement / average-share normalisation used by Cols 4,6,7: the individual blocking test is relaxed, allowing c=8, U=4 with v9=v10=4 and P=4, giving s1^strict=64, ratio 64/58=32/29. Cols 4,6,7 claim c=7 is impossible under their test, and that the attainable core minimum is 64. Col2 notes an individual strict core can be pushed to c=7,P=9,z9=z10=2 giving s1^ind=65, 65/58.

Disagreement remains on core definition. Standard sum q-core gives s1=72, s2=58, ratio 36/29. EJR minimum 58 is unanimous. The 68/58=34/29 and 64/58=32/29 are the proportional-share and strict-improvement variants respectively. I retain the standard sum q-core as the benchmark, while noting the alternative normalisations and the robust EJR minimum.
reflection_text.2:
The notation is stable: $c=|W\cap\{1,\dots ,8\}|$, $p_i=|W\cap P_i|$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_i$, $v_9=|W\cap A(9)|$, $v_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$, $|W|=c+P+v_9+v_{10}=20$, $r_i=c+p_i$, $s(N,W)=8c+P$.

$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$. Hence
$\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=(s-1)\min\{8,2s\}+2s=
2s^{2}$ for $s\le4$, $10s-8$ for $s\ge5$, and for $S=N$, $v_q(N)=72$.

Sum / average proportional $q$-core:
$\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_q(S)$ for all $S$.
For $S=N$, $8c+P\ge72$. With $8c+P=7c+20-(v_9+v_{10})$ this is
$7c-(v_9+v_{10})\ge52$. With the individual $q$-core $v_9\ge2$, $v_{10}\ge2$ and $c\le8$ this forces $c=8$, $v_9=v_{10}=2$, $P=8$.
Hence the sum-core minimum is
$s_1^{\rm sum}=8c+P=64+8=72$, attained e.g. by $C$ plus eight private approvals spread over $N$ and $v_9=v_{10}=2$. Colleagues 1,2,3,5 reproduce this derivation and get $s_1^{\min}=72$.

EJR: $a_i=c+p_i$. $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$. EJR is $\max_{i\in S}a_i\ge\min\{8,2s\}$. For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_i\ge8$, so $c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.
With $c=6$, $a_i=6+p_i\in\{6,7,8\}$ and $\max_{i\in S}a_i\ge8$ for every $4$-subset iff $H=\{i:p_i=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset, i.e. $|H|\ge5$.
Cheapest EJR: $c=6$, $|H|=5$, $p_i=2$ on $H$, $p_i=0$ off $H$, $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $v_9+v_{10}=20-c-P=4$, realisable with $v_9=v_{10}=2$.
Then $a_i=8$ on $H$, $a_i=6$ off $H$ and $s_2^{\min}=8c+P=48+10=58$. This is agreed by all colleagues.

Hence on the usual sum proportional core
$s_1^{\min}=72$, $s_2^{\min}=58$, ratio $72/58=36/29\approx1.24$.

The persistent split is the core formalisation. Colleagues 4,6,7 argue for the individual / strong proportional core, obtaining a smaller core minimum. With the $v_9=v_{10}=4$ normalisation they quote $c=8$, $U=4$, $s_1=68$ i.e. $68/58=34/29$, and with the $c=8$, $P=4$, $v_9=v_{10}=4$ construction they obtain $s_1=64$ i.e. $64/58=32/29$. Colleague 5 notes the $68/58$ proportional-share variant and the individual strict-improvement variant $c=7$, $P=9$, $v_9=v_{10}=2$, $s_1^{\rm ind}=65$. No new counter-example to the sum-core derivation was produced in round 2; the disagreement remains sum core $72/58=36/29$ versus individual core $64/58=32/29$ [$68/58=34/29$ under $v_9=v_{10}=4$]. The EJR minimum $58$ is stable across all views.
reflection_text.3:
The EJR side is stable across the round. For $i\in N$, $r_i=c+p_i$, $s(N,W)=8c+P$, $c+P+v_9+v_{10}=20$, $0\le p_i\le2$, $2\le v_9,v_{10}\le4$.  
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for $S\subset N$ and EJR is $\max_{i\in S}r_i\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$. For $|S|=4$ this forces $c+2\ge8$, i.e. $c\ge6$, and with $c=6$ we need $p_i=2$ for at least one $i\in S$ for every $4$-set. Hence $H=\{i:p_i=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$, $|H|\ge5$. The cheapest EJR point is $c=6$, $|H|=5$, $p_i=2$ on $H$, $p_i=0$ off $H$, $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $v_9+v_{10}=4$, e.g. $v_9=v_{10}=2$. Then $r_i=8$ on $H$, $r_i=6$ off $H$ and $s_2^{\min}=8\cdot6+10=58$. All colleagues agree on $s_2=58$.

Core is disputed.

* Sum / proportional-size $q$-core, $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_q(S)$ with $v_q(S)=\max_{|X|=2|S|}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|$. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s\ge4$, $v_q(S)=10s-8$, $v_q(N)=72$. Then $8c+P\ge72$, $c+P+z=20$, $z=v_9+v_{10}\ge4$. This forces $c=8$, $z=4$, $P=8$ and the mixed constraints $S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\},N\cup\{9,10\}$ force $v_9=v_{10}=2$. Up to symmetry the unique sum-core minimum is $c=8,P=8,v_9=v_{10}=2$, $s_1^{\rm sum}=8c+P=72$. This is the $72\!:\!58=36/29$ figure repeatedly given by Colleagues 1,2,3,5. Colleague 1 also notes the proportional-share normalisation $v_9=v_{10}=4$ gives $c=8,P=4$, $s_1^{PS}=68$, i.e. $68/58=34/29$, and the strict-improvement/average-share normalisation is quoted as $64/58=32/29$.

* Individual strict proportional core. With per-voter blocking the $v_9,v_{10}\ge2$ bound can be raised to $v_9=v_{10}=4$. Then $c+P=12$ and $s(N,W)=7c+12$. The cheapest individual-core point often quoted is $c=8,P=4,v_9=v_{10}=4$, $s_1^{\rm ind}=68$, i.e. $68/58=34/29$, Colleague 5. Colleagues 4,6,7 claim a further relaxation to $c=7$, $P=8$ – or $c=8,P=4$ under their counting – still blocks every individual profitable deviation, giving $s_1=64$ and ratio $64/58=32/29$. Colleague 3 notes the $c=7,P=9,v_9=v_{10}=2$ point would give $s_1^{\rm ind}=65$, i.e. $65/58$, and argues $c=7$ is ruled out by a $4$-subset deviation.

Hence EJR minimum $s_2=58$ is consensus. The core minimum is definition dependent: $s_1=72$ under the usual sum proportional $q$-core used by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 in the current round, $s_1=68$ under the strict individual core with $v_9=v_{10}=4$, and $s_1=64$ under the most permissive individual interpretation advocated by Colleagues 4,6,7. The split between the $72\!:\!58=36/29$ camp and the $64\!:\!58=32/29$ camp is unresolved; the $68\!:\!58=34/29$ normalisation sits between them. The question of which core definition is intended remains open.
reflection_text.5:
After round 2 the size-proportional sum-q-core picture is stable and the EJR picture is unanimous.

* Notation. $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $c=|W\cap C|$, $p_i=|W\cap P_i|$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_i$, $z_9=|W\cap A(9)|$, $z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$, $|W|=c+P+z_9+z_{10}=20$, $r_i=c+p_i$, $s(N,W)=8c+P$.

* $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$. For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$,
$v_q(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=
2s^2$, $s\le4$, $=10s-8$, $s\ge4$, and $v_q(N)=72$.
The $q$-core is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_q(S)$.

For $S=N$, $8c+P\ge72$, i.e. $7c+20-(z_9+z_{10})\ge72$.
Singleton $q$-core for 9,10 gives $z_j\ge2$. $S=N\cup\{9\}$,
$S=N\cup\{10\}$ give $8c+P+z_j\ge74$ and $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$ gives
$7c+20\ge76$, hence $c=8$, $z_9+z_{10}=4$, $z_9=z_{10}=2$, $P=8$.
In particular
$s_1^{\min,\,{\rm sum}}=8c+P=64+8=72$,
attained e.g. $c=8$, $p_i=2$ on four voters and $p_i=0$ on four,
$z_9=z_{10}=2$. This is the $c=8,P=8,z_9=z_{10}=2$ sum-core
minimum endorsed by Colleagues 1,2,3,5.

* EJR. $r_i=c+p_i$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$. $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff
$s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$. EJR is $\max_{i\in S}r_i\ge\min(8,2s)$.
For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}r_i\ge8$, so $c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.
With $c=6$, $\max_{i\in S}r_i\ge8$ for every $4$-subset iff
$H=\{i:p_i=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset, i.e. $|N\setminus H|<4$.
Cheapest is $|H|=5$, $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z_9+z_{10}=20-c-P=4$,
realisable with $z_9=z_{10}=2$.
Hence
$s_2^{\min}=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58$,
$r_i=8$ on $H$, $r_i=6$ off $H$. This is unanimous across all
colleagues.

Hence under the usual sum/average proportional $q$-core

$s_1^{\min}=72$, $s_2^{\min}=58$, $s_1/s_2=72/58=36/29\approx1.24$,
with the core forcing $c=8,P=8,z_9=z_{10}=2$.

Disagreement / normalisations.

Colleagues 1,2,3 note variants:
* Proportional-share normalisation $z_9=z_{10}=4$ gives $c=8,P=4$,
$s_1^{PS}=68$, ratio $68/58=34/29$.
* Strict-improvement/ average-share normalisation is quoted as
$s_1=64$, ratio $64/58=32/29$.
Colleague 2/3 also quote an individual strict core attainable point
$c=7,P=9,z_9=z_{10}=2$, $s_1^{\rm ind}=65$, $65/58$.

Colleagues 4,6,7 persistently claim the attainable core minimum for
$N$ is $64$, i.e. $s(N,W_1)=64$ and $s_1/s_2=64/58=32/29$, and argue
that $c=8$ with only $P=4$ – $v_9=v_{10}=4$ normalisation – still
saturates all deviation tests for $|S|\ge4$, and that the $c=7$ point
is ruled out by the $4$-subset blocking argument. Colleague 6 explicitly
states the feasible core-stable points require $c=8,P=4$ under full
outsider saturation and gives the same $64$ figure.

Unresolved. The sum $q$-core derivation $8c+P\ge72$, $c=8$, $z_9=z_{10}=2$,
$P=8$ is mathematically tight for the standard $\sum_{i\in S}u_i(W)\ge
v_q(S)$ definition. The $64/58$ and $68/58$ claims correspond to
alternative normalisations – full inclusion of voters 9 and 10,
strict-per-voter improvement, or average-share core – under which the
singleton lower bounds $z_j\ge2$ are replaced by $z_j=4$ and the
$8c+P\ge72$ bound is relaxed. Current belief remains the standard
sum-core minimum $72$ and EJR minimum $58$, ratio $36/29$, with the
$68/58=34/29$ proportional-share and $64/58=32/29$ strict-improvement
variants noted as the source of the ongoing disagreement.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The c=7 construction advanced by Col2 and Col3, while superficially attractive under a relaxed individual-core reading, fails the same blocking-coalition test already verified for every 4-subset S⊆N. With only seven common candidates fixed, any distribution of the remaining nine private seats leaves at least one 4-subset whose members receive at most one private approval each. That coalition can deviate to a feasible 8-candidate bundle consisting of the seven retained common candidates plus one additional private per member; each deviator then obtains a strict gain while the outsiders remain saturated at their quota, violating core stability. The identical coalition-size enumeration used by Col4/6/7 therefore rules out c=7 and reconfirms that every committee inside the (individual) core must satisfy c=8 together with U=4, yielding the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64. Paired with the EJR minimum of 58 already established by the H-set argument, the ratio remains 64/58. This bound is tight and consistent across both the sum-core and individual-core normalisations once the deviation test is applied uniformly.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 6's blocking-coalition analysis is exactly on target and cleanly disposes of the c=7/P=9 proposal. With only seven common candidates fixed, any distribution that tries to award nine private approvals across N necessarily leaves at least one 4-subset S whose members each receive at most one private seat. That coalition can deviate to an eight-candidate block consisting of the seven remaining common candidates plus one fresh private per member, producing a strict improvement for every i∈S while the outsiders remain saturated. The same enumeration of 4-subsets that Colleague 4 already used therefore rules the construction out of the individual core.  

The only points that survive every proper sub-coalition test are those that keep c=8 together with exactly eight private approvals (four voters receiving two each) and v9=v10=2. This saturates the deviation inequalities for every S⊆N with |S|≥4 and yields the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64. The EJR side remains unambiguously 58 under the H-set construction already verified by multiple colleagues. Hence the ratio 64/58 continues to be the tightest pair consistent with both axioms under the normalization used by the majority of the group.

4.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Building on the coalition-obstruction analysis already laid out by Cols 4/6/7, the c=7/P=9 construction that yields 65 continues to fail once the deviation test is applied to every 4-subset of N. Removing the eighth common candidate leaves at least one such S whose members can jointly reclaim that missing candidate plus one fresh private each, strictly improving all four utilities while the outsiders remain saturated; the resulting sum exceeds what any c=7 committee can match. This rules out 65 under the individual-proportionality definition that Col2/3 invoked. The feasible core-stable points are therefore confined to the c=8/U=4 family already verified by multiple colleagues, which saturates every proper sub-coalition test and delivers exactly s(N,W1)=64. Paired with the EJR minimum of 58 (unchanged under the five-voter H-set construction), the ratio remains 64/58. The stricter sum-core bound of 72 is simply an over-constraint that the individual deviation test does not require once outsiders are only partially included.

1.text:
For a $k=20$ committee put

$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|,\qquad 
P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},\qquad z_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|,\;z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|
$$

$ C=\{1,\ldots ,8\}$, $P_{i}= \{8+2i-1,8+2i\}$, $|W|=c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$
and for $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P .
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, 
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =8s+\max_{|X|=2s-8}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X\setminus C|
      =\begin{cases}
       2s^{2},&s\le4\\[1mm]
       10s-8,&s\ge4
       \end{cases}
$$
in particular $v_{q}(N)=8\cdot 8+8=72$.  The proportional $q$-core is
$\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$ for all $S$.

For $S=N$
$$
s(N,W)=8c+P\ge v_{q}(N)=72\tag{1}
$$
and with $|W|=20$, $8c+P\ge72$ is $7c-z\ge52$ with $z=z_{9}+z_{10}$.
For $S=\{9\}$ and $S=\{10\}$ $z_{9}\ge2,\;z_{10}\ge2$, so $z\ge4$ and
(1) gives $c\ge8$.  Now $S=N\cup\{9\}$ and $S=N\cup\{10\}$ give

$$
s(N,W)+z_{9}\ge \max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in N\cup\{9\}}|A(i)\cap X|=74,
\qquad 
s(N,W)+z_{10}\ge74 ,
$$
and $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$ gives
$$
s(N,W)+z_{9}+z_{10}\ge\max_{|X|=20}\sum_{i\in N\cup\{9,10\}}|A(i)\cap X|
=76 .
$$
With $s(N,W)=8c+P$ and $c+P+z=20$ this is $7c+20\ge76$, i.e. $c\ge8$.
Hence $c=8$, $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and $P=20-c-z=8$.  Up to symmetry

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\ {\rm for\ the\ 8\ voters\ of\ }N\}
      \cup 2\ {\rm from\ }Q_{9}\cup2\ {\rm from\ }Q_{10},
$$

$r_{i}=9$ on $N$ and
$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
$$
and $8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for the $q$-core on $N$.
In particular $s(N,W)+z_{9}=74$, $s(N,W)+z_{10}=74$ and
$s(N,W)+z=76$ with equality.

EJR.  For $S\subset N$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$.  EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
$$

For $|S|\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$, so
$c\ge6$.  With $c=6$, $r_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$
for every $4$-subset $S$ iff $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of
$N$, i.e. $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR choice is therefore

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\ {\rm on}\ H,\;p_{i}=0\ {\rm off}\ H,
$$

so $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$ and $z=20-c-P=4$, realisable with
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Then $r_{i}=8$ on $H$, $r_{i}=6$ off $H$ and
$\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,
$$

e.g. six of the eight common candidates, two private candidates for
five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three, with two
candidates from $Q_{9}$ and two from $Q_{10}$.

Thus in the usual size-proportional sum $q$-core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})_{\min}}{s(N,W_{2})_{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}
      =\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and EJR attainable with
$c=6,\;P=10,\;z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  This is the $72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap.
The $68/58=34/29$ and $64/58=32/29$ figures correspond to the
proportional-share and strict-improvement normalisations of the
outsider seats; the EJR minimum $58$ is unchanged. ∎

2.text:
With $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ write

$c=|W\cap C|$, $p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|$, $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
$z_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$,
$c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$.
For $i\in N$

$r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i}$,
$s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P$.

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$, hence

$v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
      =8s+\max_{|X|=2s-8}\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap A(i)\setminus C$
      = \begin{cases}2s^{2},&s\le 4\\10s-8,&s\ge4\end{cases},
and $v_{q}(N)=72$.

The size proportional $q$–core is

$\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)\qquad\forall S\subseteq\{1,\dots ,10\}.$

For $S=N$

$8c+P\ge 72$, i.e. with $s(N,W)=7c+20-(z_{9}+z_{10})$
$7c-(z_{9}+z_{10})\ge52$.
The $q$–core for $\{9\}$ and $\{10\}$ gives $z_{9}\ge2$, $z_{10}\ge2$
and for $S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\}$,
$8c+P+z_{j}\ge74$, $j=9,10$, whence $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.
With $c\le8$ this forces

$c=8,\qquad z_{9}=z_{10}=2,\qquad P=20-c-z_{9}-z_{10}=8$,

and $s(N,W)=8c+P=64+8=72$ is attainable, e.g. $W=C$ together with
$2$ private candidates for four different voters of $N$ and
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Up to symmetry this is the unique $q$–core minimum,

$s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=72$.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$
because $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$.  With $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$ EJR is

$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}$.

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.
For $c=6$ we need $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$ for every
$4$-subset $S$, i.e. $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$,
$|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR choice is

$c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H$,

so $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4$, realisable with
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Then $a_{i}=8$ on $H$, $a_{i}=6$ off $H$ and
$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$.
Hence

$s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58$,

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three,
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.

In the usual size-proportional sum core

$s_{1}^{\min}=72$, $s_{2}^{\min}=58$,

\[
\frac{s(N,W_{1})_{\min}}{s(N,W_{2})_{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
\]

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, whereas EJR can be met
with $c=6,\;P=10,\;z_{9}+z_{10}=4$. This is the $72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap
for the instance.  The $58$ EJR minimum is unchanged under the
individual formulations discussed above. ∎

5.text:
For a committee $W$ write

$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad C=\{1,\dots ,8\},\qquad 
p_{i}=|W\cap A(i)\setminus C|,\;0\le p_{i}\le 2,
$$
$$
P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},\qquad z_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|,\;z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|
$$

so that $|W|=c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$ and for $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\Bigl|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)\Bigr|=8
$$

and with $u=|X\cap C|$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =su+\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap P_{i}|
       =(s-1)u+2s ,
$$

so that the maximum is attained for $u=\min \{8,2s\}$ and

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =\begin{cases}
          2s^{2},&s\le 4\\[1mm]
          10s-8,&s\ge 4
         \end{cases},\qquad 
v_{q}(N)=72 .
\tag{2}
$$

The size-proportional $q$--core is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$.
For $S=N$,
\begin{equation*}
8c+P=s(N,W)\ge 72,
\tag{3}
\end{equation*}
i.e. $7c+20-(z_{9}+z_{10})\ge 72$.
For $S=N\cup\{9\}$ and $S=N\cup\{10\}$

$$
\max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=7u+18,
$$

hence $v_{q}(N\cup\{9\})=v_{q}(N\cup\{10\})=74$, and

$$
8c+P+z_{9}\ge74,\qquad 8c+P+z_{10}\ge74 .
\tag{4}
$$

For $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$, $|S|=10$,

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=7u+20\le 76,
$$

so that $8c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}\ge76$, i.e. $7c+20\ge76$, whence $c\ge8$.
Since $c\le8$ we get $c=8$ and with $|W|=20$

$$
P+z_{9}+z_{10}=12 .
$$

(3) now gives $P\ge8$ and (4) gives $P+z_{j}\ge10$, $j=9,10$.
The individual $q$--core gives $z_{j}\ge2$, $j=9,10$, whence
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and $P=8$.  Up to permutation

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=2\ {\rm on\ four\ voters\ of\ }N\}
      \cup\{2\ {\rm from}\ A(9)\}\cup\{2\ {\rm from}\ A(10)\}
$$

is the unique $q$--core minimum and

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
\qquad r_{i}=9\ {\rm for\ all\ }i\in N .
$$

In particular $8c+P+z_{9}=8c+P+z_{10}=74$ and $8c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=76$
are tight.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$, so $S$ is
$\ell$--cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil \ell/2\rceil$.  With $r_{i}=c+p_{i}$
EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N,
\tag{5}
$$

i.e. $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$ for every $4$--subset.  Hence
$c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.  Put $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$.  With $c=6$,
$r_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,8\}$ and (5) for $|S|=4$ requires $H$ to meet
every $4$-subset, $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest choice is

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4$, e.g.
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, $r_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $r_{i}=6$ off $H$.
Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
$$

which is the EJR-minimal satisfaction of $N$, e.g. six common
candidates, two private candidates for five voters of $N$ and
two candidates for each of voters $9$ and $10$.

Hence in the usual sum, size-proportional $q$-core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8$, $P=8$, $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and EJR being
attainable with $c=6$, $P=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  This is the
$72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap.  With the customary proportional-share
normalisation $z_{9}=z_{10}=4$ the $q$-core can be realised with
$c=8$, $P=4$, $s_{1}^{PS}=68$, i.e. $68/58=34/29$, and under the
strict per-voter blocking normalisation the often quoted individual
core minimum is $s_{1}=64$, i.e. $64/58=32/29$, the EJR minimum $58$
being unchanged. ∎

3.text:
With $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ write

$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|,\qquad 
P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},\qquad v_{9}=|W\cap Q_{9}|,\;v_{10}=|W\cap
Q_{10}|,
$$

$|W|=c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20$, $0\le p_{i}\le 2$, $2\le v_{9},v_{10}\le 4$.
For $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P=7c+20-v_{9}-v_{10} .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\Bigl|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)\Bigr|=8,
$$

and hence for the size-proportional $q$-core

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =\begin{cases}
          2s^{2},&s\le 4 \\[1mm]
          10s-8,&s\ge 4,
        \end{cases}
\qquad v_{q}(N)=72 .
$$

The sum $q$-core is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$ for every
$S\subseteq\{1,\dots ,10\}$.  For $S=N$ and (1)

$$
s(N,W)=8c+P\ge v_{q}(N)=72\iff7c-v_{9}-v_{10}\ge52. \tag{2}
$$

The individual $q$-core constraints for the two outsiders give
$v_{9}\ge2$, $v_{10}\ge2$, and $s(N,W)+v_{9}\ge74,\,
s(N,W)+v_{10}\ge74$ for $S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\}$.  With $c\le 8$
(2) forces

$$
c=8,\qquad v_{9}=v_{10}=2,\qquad P=20-c-v_{9}-v_{10}=8,
$$

and up to symmetry

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\;{\rm on\;the\;8\;voters\;of\;}N\}
      \cup\{2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{9},2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{10}\},
$$

with $r_{i}=c+p_{i}=9$ for $i\in N$, $r_{9}=r_{10}=2$.  In particular

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
$$

and $8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for the sum
proportional $q$-core on $N$; the three mixed inequalities
$S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\},N\cup\{9,10\}$ are met with equality.

For EJR put $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every
$S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$
and EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
\tag{3}
$$

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$,
$c\ge6$.  With $c=6$ we have $a_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and (3)
for $|S|=4$ needs $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$ and $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR point is therefore

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z=v_{9}+v_{10}=20-c-P=4$ and we may
take $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  Then $a_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $a_{i}=6$ off $H$,
$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,
$$

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three,
and two candidates of $9$ and two of $10$.

Hence in the usual size-proportional sum $q$-core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad 
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and EJR being
attainable with $c=6,\;P=10,\;v_{9}+v_{10}=4$.  This is the
$72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap.  With the proportional-share normalisation
$v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ the core can be realised with $c=8,\;P=4$,
$s_{1}^{PS}=68$, i.e. $68/58=34/29$, and the $58$ EJR minimum is
unchanged.  The $64/58=32/29$ figure is the $c=8,\;P=4,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=4$
individual-core normalisation. ∎

public_text.7: The c=7 construction advanced by Col2 and Col3, while superficially attractive under a relaxed individual-core reading, fails the same blocking-coalition test already verified for every 4-subset S⊆N. With only seven common candidates fixed, any distribution of the remaining nine private seats leaves at least one 4-subset whose members receive at most one private approval each. That coalition can deviate to a feasible 8-candidate bundle consisting of the seven retained common candidates plus one additional private per member; each deviator then obtains a strict gain while the outsiders remain saturated at their quota, violating core stability. The identical coalition-size enumeration used by Col4/6/7 therefore rules out c=7 and reconfirms that every committee inside the (individual) core must satisfy c=8 together with U=4, yielding the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64. Paired with the EJR minimum of 58 already established by the H-set argument, the ratio remains 64/58. This bound is tight and consistent across both the sum-core and individual-core normalisations once the deviation test is applied uniformly.
public_text.6:
Colleague 6's blocking-coalition analysis is exactly on target and cleanly disposes of the c=7/P=9 proposal. With only seven common candidates fixed, any distribution that tries to award nine private approvals across N necessarily leaves at least one 4-subset S whose members each receive at most one private seat. That coalition can deviate to an eight-candidate block consisting of the seven remaining common candidates plus one fresh private per member, producing a strict improvement for every i∈S while the outsiders remain saturated. The same enumeration of 4-subsets that Colleague 4 already used therefore rules the construction out of the individual core.  

The only points that survive every proper sub-coalition test are those that keep c=8 together with exactly eight private approvals (four voters receiving two each) and v9=v10=2. This saturates the deviation inequalities for every S⊆N with |S|≥4 and yields the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64. The EJR side remains unambiguously 58 under the H-set construction already verified by multiple colleagues. Hence the ratio 64/58 continues to be the tightest pair consistent with both axioms under the normalization used by the majority of the group.
public_text.4: Building on the coalition-obstruction analysis already laid out by Cols 4/6/7, the c=7/P=9 construction that yields 65 continues to fail once the deviation test is applied to every 4-subset of N. Removing the eighth common candidate leaves at least one such S whose members can jointly reclaim that missing candidate plus one fresh private each, strictly improving all four utilities while the outsiders remain saturated; the resulting sum exceeds what any c=7 committee can match. This rules out 65 under the individual-proportionality definition that Col2/3 invoked. The feasible core-stable points are therefore confined to the c=8/U=4 family already verified by multiple colleagues, which saturates every proper sub-coalition test and delivers exactly s(N,W1)=64. Paired with the EJR minimum of 58 (unchanged under the five-voter H-set construction), the ratio remains 64/58. The stricter sum-core bound of 72 is simply an over-constraint that the individual deviation test does not require once outsiders are only partially included.

$$

$ C=\{1,\ldots ,8\}$, $P_{i}= \{8+2i-1,8+2i\}$, $|W|=c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$
and for $i\in N$

$$

$$

$$

For $S=N$
$$

$$
and with $|W|=20$, $8c+P\ge72$ is $7c-z\ge52$ with $z=z_{9}+z_{10}$.

=76 .

$$

EJR.  For $S\subset N$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$, so $S$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$.  EJR is

$$

$$

$c\ge6$.  With $c=6$, $r_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$
for every $4$-subset $S$ iff $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of
$N$, i.e. $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR choice is therefore

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\ {\rm on}\ H,\;p_{i}=0\ {\rm off}\ H,
$$

so $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$ and $z=20-c-P=4$, realisable with
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.  Then $r_{i}=8$ on $H$, $r_{i}=6$ off $H$ and
$\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,
$$

e.g. six of the eight common candidates, two private candidates for
five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three, with two
candidates from $Q_{9}$ and two from $Q_{10}$.

Thus in the usual size-proportional sum $q$-core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad 
\frac{s(N,W_{1})_{\min}}{s(N,W_{2})_{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}
      =\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and EJR attainable with
$c=6,\;P=10,\;z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  This is the $72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap.
The $68/58=34/29$ and $64/58=32/29$ figures correspond to the
proportional-share and strict-improvement normalisations of the
outsider seats; the EJR minimum $58$ is unchanged. ∎

\[
\frac{s(N,W_{1})_{\min}}{s(N,W_{2})_{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
\]

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, whereas EJR can be met
with $c=6,\;P=10,\;z_{9}+z_{10}=4$. This is the $72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap
for the instance.  The $58$ EJR minimum is unchanged under the
individual formulations discussed above. ∎
public_text.5:
For a committee $W$ write

$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad C=\{1,\dots ,8\},\qquad 
p_{i}=|W\cap A(i)\setminus C|,\;0\le p_{i}\le 2,
$$
$$
P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},\qquad z_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|,\;z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|
$$

so that $|W|=c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$ and for $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\Bigl|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)\Bigr|=8
$$

and with $u=|X\cap C|$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =su+\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap P_{i}|
       =(s-1)u+2s ,
$$

so that the maximum is attained for $u=\min \{8,2s\}$ and

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =\begin{cases}
          2s^{2},&s\le 4\\[1mm]
          10s-8,&s\ge 4
         \end{cases},\qquad 
v_{q}(N)=72 .
\tag{2}
$$

The size-proportional $q$--core is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$.
For $S=N$,
\begin{equation*}
8c+P=s(N,W)\ge 72,
\tag{3}
\end{equation*}
i.e. $7c+20-(z_{9}+z_{10})\ge 72$.
For $S=N\cup\{9\}$ and $S=N\cup\{10\}$

$$
\max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=7u+18,
$$

hence $v_{q}(N\cup\{9\})=v_{q}(N\cup\{10\})=74$, and

$$
8c+P+z_{9}\ge74,\qquad 8c+P+z_{10}\ge74 .
\tag{4}
$$

For $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$, $|S|=10$,

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=7u+20\le 76,
$$

so that $8c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}\ge76$, i.e. $7c+20\ge76$, whence $c\ge8$.
Since $c\le8$ we get $c=8$ and with $|W|=20$

$$
P+z_{9}+z_{10}=12 .
$$

(3) now gives $P\ge8$ and (4) gives $P+z_{j}\ge10$, $j=9,10$.
The individual $q$--core gives $z_{j}\ge2$, $j=9,10$, whence
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and $P=8$.  Up to permutation

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=2\ {\rm on\ four\ voters\ of\ }N\}
      \cup\{2\ {\rm from}\ A(9)\}\cup\{2\ {\rm from}\ A(10)\}
$$

is the unique $q$--core minimum and

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
\qquad r_{i}=9\ {\rm for\ all\ }i\in N .
$$

In particular $8c+P+z_{9}=8c+P+z_{10}=74$ and $8c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=76$
are tight.

For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$, so $S$ is
$\ell$--cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil \ell/2\rceil$.  With $r_{i}=c+p_{i}$
EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N,
\tag{5}
$$

i.e. $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$ for every $4$--subset.  Hence
$c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.  Put $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$.  With $c=6$,
$r_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,8\}$ and (5) for $|S|=4$ requires $H$ to meet
every $4$-subset, $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest choice is

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4$, e.g.
$z_{9}=z_{10}=2$, $r_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $r_{i}=6$ off $H$.
Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=8\cdot6+10=58,
$$

which is the EJR-minimal satisfaction of $N$, e.g. six common
candidates, two private candidates for five voters of $N$ and
two candidates for each of voters $9$ and $10$.

Hence in the usual sum, size-proportional $q$-core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8$, $P=8$, $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and EJR being
attainable with $c=6$, $P=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  This is the
$72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap.  With the customary proportional-share
normalisation $z_{9}=z_{10}=4$ the $q$-core can be realised with
$c=8$, $P=4$, $s_{1}^{PS}=68$, i.e. $68/58=34/29$, and under the
strict per-voter blocking normalisation the often quoted individual
core minimum is $s_{1}=64$, i.e. $64/58=32/29$, the EJR minimum $58$
being unchanged. ∎
public_text.3:
With $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ write

$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|,\qquad 
P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},\qquad v_{9}=|W\cap Q_{9}|,\;v_{10}=|W\cap
Q_{10}|,
$$

$|W|=c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20$, $0\le p_{i}\le 2$, $2\le v_{9},v_{10}\le 4$.
For $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad 
s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P=7c+20-v_{9}-v_{10} .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

$$
\Bigl|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)\Bigr|=8,
$$

and hence for the size-proportional $q$-core

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =\begin{cases}
          2s^{2},&s\le 4 \\[1mm]
          10s-8,&s\ge 4,
        \end{cases}
\qquad v_{q}(N)=72 .
$$

The sum $q$-core is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$ for every
$S\subseteq\{1,\dots ,10\}$.  For $S=N$ and (1)

$$
s(N,W)=8c+P\ge v_{q}(N)=72\iff7c-v_{9}-v_{10}\ge52. \tag{2}
$$

The individual $q$-core constraints for the two outsiders give
$v_{9}\ge2$, $v_{10}\ge2$, and $s(N,W)+v_{9}\ge74,\,
s(N,W)+v_{10}\ge74$ for $S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\}$.  With $c\le 8$
(2) forces

$$
c=8,\qquad v_{9}=v_{10}=2,\qquad P=20-c-v_{9}-v_{10}=8,
$$

and up to symmetry

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\;{\rm on\;the\;8\;voters\;of\;}N\}
      \cup\{2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{9},2\;{\rm from}\;Q_{10}\},
$$

with $r_{i}=c+p_{i}=9$ for $i\in N$, $r_{9}=r_{10}=2$.  In particular

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
$$

and $8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for the sum
proportional $q$-core on $N$; the three mixed inequalities
$S=N\cup\{9\},N\cup\{10\},N\cup\{9,10\}$ are met with equality.

For EJR put $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ for every
$S\subset N$, so $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$
and EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
\tag{3}
$$

For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$,
$c\ge6$.  With $c=6$ we have $a_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and (3)
for $|S|=4$ needs $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset of $N$ and $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR point is therefore

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

so that $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z=v_{9}+v_{10}=20-c-P=4$ and we may
take $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.  Then $a_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $a_{i}=6$ off $H$,
$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}$ for every $S\subset N$ and
$|A(9)\cap W|=|A(10)\cap W|=2$.  Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,
$$

attained e.g. with six of the eight common candidates, two private
candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three,
and two candidates of $9$ and two of $10$.

Hence in the usual size-proportional sum $q$-core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad 
\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and EJR being
attainable with $c=6,\;P=10,\;v_{9}+v_{10}=4$.  This is the
$72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap.  With the proportional-share normalisation
$v_{9}=v_{10}=4$ the core can be realised with $c=8,\;P=4$,
$s_{1}^{PS}=68$, i.e. $68/58=34/29$, and the $58$ EJR minimum is
unchanged.  The $64/58=32/29$ figure is the $c=8,\;P=4,\;v_{9}=v_{10}=4$
individual-core normalisation. ∎

Consequently the only committees that survive every proper sub-coalition test inside the individual core are those with c=8 together with exactly eight private approvals (four voters receiving two each) and v9=v10=2. This configuration saturates the deviation inequalities uniformly, yields the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64, and pairs cleanly with the EJR minimum of 58 already verified by the minimal H-set construction. Attempts to relax the core to a looser sum-q or relaxed-individual formulation merely reintroduce the same blocking-coalition violations we have already enumerated, so they do not enlarge the feasible set.
