2.text:
For $C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$ put $c=|W\cap C|$, $p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|$,
$P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$, $v_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|$, $v_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|$.
Then $|W|=c+P+v_{9}+v_{10}=20$ and for $i\in N$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P
      =7c+20-v_{9}-v_{10} .
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and with $u=|X\cap C|$

$$
\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|=su+\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap P_{i}|
      =(s-1)u+2s ,
$$

so that the size proportional $q$–value is

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
 =\begin{cases}
   2s^{2},&s\le4\\[1mm]
   10s-8,&s\ge4
  \end{cases},
\qquad v_{q}(N)=8\cdot8+8=72 .
$$

The size proportional $q$–core is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$
for every $S$.  For $S=N$

$$
s(N,W)=8c+P\ge v_{q}(N)=72\tag{1}
$$

and $s(N,W)=7c+20-(v_{9}+v_{10})$.  For the two outsiders
$v_{j}\ge q(\{j\})=2$, $j=9,10$, and

$$
\max_{|X|=18}\sum_{i\in N\cup\{j\}}|A(i)\cap X|=74,
\qquad 
\max_{|X|=20}\sum_{i\in N\cup\{9,10\}}|A(i)\cap X|=76,
$$

i.e. in the $q$–core

$$
s(N,W)+v_{9}\ge74,\qquad s(N,W)+v_{10}\ge74,\qquad
s(N,W)+v_{9}+v_{10}\ge76 .
\tag{2}
$$

With (1) and (2) $7c+20-(v_{9}+v_{10})\ge72$ gives $7c\ge52+v_{9}+v_{10}$,
$v_{9}+v_{10}\ge4$ and $7c+20\ge76$.  Hence $c\ge8$ and $c\le8$ gives

$$
c=8,\qquad v_{9}+v_{10}=4,\qquad s(N,W)=7\cdot8+20-4=72 .
$$

The individual $q$–conditions $v_{j}\ge2$ then force $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ and
$P=20-c-v_{9}-v_{10}=8$.  Up to permutation

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\;{\rm on\;the\;eight\;voters\;of\;}N\}
      \cup2{\rm\;from\;}A(9)\cup2{\rm\;from\;}A(10)
$$

is the $q$–core minimum and

$$
r_{i}=c+p_{i}=9\;\forall i\in N,\qquad 
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
$$
with $s(N,W)+v_{9}=s(N,W)+v_{10}=74$ and
$s(N,W)+v_{9}+v_{10}=76$ tight.  In particular $8c+P\ge72$ is
necessary and sufficient for the sum $q$–core on $N$.

For EJR let $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ so $S\subset N$
is $\ell$-cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$, $\ell\le8$.  EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}\quad\forall S\subset N .
$$

For $|S|\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$ and
$c\ge6$.  With $c=6$, $a_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and the condition for
$|S|=4$ is $p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence
$H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ must meet every $4$-subset of $N$, $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR choice is

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

so $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $v_{9}+v_{10}=20-c-P=4$, e.g. $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$.
Then $a_{i}=8$ on $H$, $a_{i}=6$ off $H$ and EJR holds with equality.
Hence

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,
$$

e.g. six of the eight common candidates, two private candidates for
five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three, with two
candidates from $A(9)$ and two from $A(10)$.

Consequently in the usual size-proportional sum $q$–core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})_{\min}}{s(N,W_{2})_{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}
      =\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,
$$

i.e. the core forces $c=8$, $P=8$, $v_{9}=v_{10}=2$ whereas EJR can be
met with $c=6$, $P=10$, $v_{9}+v_{10}=4$.  This is the $72\!:\!58$ core/
EJR gap.  The $58$ EJR minimum is unchanged under the individual
normalisations discussed. ∎

$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =\begin{cases}2s^{2},&s\le 4\\10s-8,&s\ge 4\end{cases},
\qquad v_{q}(N)=72 .
$$

The size proportional $q$-core is $\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$.
For $S=N$

$$
8c+P\ge 72\tag{1}
$$

and for the two outsiders $z_{9}\ge2$, $z_{10}\ge2$.  Moreover

$$
\begin{aligned}
v_{q}(N\cup\{9\})&=74, & s(N,W)+z_{9}&\ge74,\\
v_{q}(N\cup\{10\})&=74, & s(N,W)+z_{10}&\ge74,\\
v_{q}(N\cup\{9,10\})&=76, & s(N,W)+z_{9}+z_{10}&\ge76 .
\end{aligned}
$$

With $s(N,W)=7c+20-z_{9}-z_{10}$ the last inequality is $7c+20\ge76$, i.e.
$c\ge8$, and $c\le8$.  Hence

$$
c=8,\qquad 7c-z_{9}-z_{10}\ge52,
$$

and from $s(N,W)+z_{j}\ge74$ we get $z_{j}\le2$.  Together with the
individual $q$-core $z_{j}\ge2$,

$$
z_{9}=z_{10}=2,\qquad P=20-c-z_{9}-z_{10}=8,
$$

and (1) is tight.  Up to symmetry

$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\ {\rm on\ the\ eight\ voters\ of\ }N\}\cup
2{\rm\ from\ }A(9)\cup2{\rm\ from\ }A(10)
$$

and $r_{i}=9$ on $N$,

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
\qquad s(N,W)+z_{9}=s(N,W)+z_{10}=74,\;
s(N,W)+z_{9}+z_{10}=76,
$$

so $8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for the sum $q$-core on
$N$.

For $S\subset N$, $S$ is $\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$
and EJR is

$$
\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}\quad\forall S\subset N .
$$

For $|S|\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c\ge6$.  With
$c=6$, $r_{i}=6+p_{i}$ and $\max_{i\in S}r_{i}\ge8$ for every
$4$-subset iff $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets every $4$-subset, $|H|\ge5$.
The cheapest EJR point is therefore

$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\;{\rm on}\;H,\;p_{i}=0\;{\rm off}\;H,
$$

hence $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4$, e.g. $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$,
$r_{i}=8$ on $H$ and $r_{i}=6$ off $H$.  Thus

$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,
$$

e.g. six of the eight common candidates, two private candidates for
five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three, with two
candidates from $A(9)$ and two from $A(10)$.

Hence in the usual size proportional sum $q$-core

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,
\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})_{\min}}{s(N,W_{2})_{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}
\approx1.24,
$$

the core forcing $c=8,\;P=8,\;z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and EJR being attainable
with $c=6,\;P=10,\;z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  The $68/58=34/29$ and
$64/58=32/29$ figures are the proportional-share and full-outsider
saturation normalisations of the outsider seats; the EJR minimum $58$
is invariant. ∎

With
$C=\{1,\dots ,8\}$, $P_{i}=\{8+2i-1,8+2i\}$ and
$$
c=|W\cap C|,\qquad p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|,\qquad P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i},
\qquad z_{9}=|W\cap A(9)|,\;z_{10}=|W\cap A(10)|,
$$

$$
r_{i}=|A(i)\cap W|=c+p_{i},\qquad s(N,W)=\sum_{i\in N}r_{i}=8c+P .
\tag{1}
$$

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$,

      =(s-1)u+2s ,
$$
so that, up to the factor $2s-8$ private seats,
$$
v_{q}(S)=\max_{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
        =\begin{cases}
           2s^{2},&s\le4\\[1mm]
           10s-8,&s\ge4
          \end{cases},\qquad 
v_{q}(N)=72 .
$$
The size-proportional $q$–core is
$\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)$ for every $S$.

For $S=N$ (1) gives
$$
8c+P\ge v_{q}(N)=72\tag{2}
$$
i.e. $7c-z\ge52$ with $z=z_{9}+z_{10}$.
For $S=\{9\},\{10\}$ $z_{9}\ge2,\;z_{10}\ge2$ and
$$
v_{q}(N\cup\{9\})=v_{q}(N\cup\{10\})=74,
\qquad v_{q}(N\cup\{9,10\})=76,
$$
hence
$$
s(N,W)+z_{9}\ge74,\qquad s(N,W)+z_{10}\ge74,
\qquad s(N,W)+z_{9}+z_{10}\ge76 .
\tag{3}
$$
With $c\le8$ (2)–(3) give $c=8$.  Then $P+z_{9}+z_{10}=12$ and
(2) gives $P\ge8$; (3) gives $P+z_{j}\ge10$.  With $z_{j}\ge2$ this
forces
$$
c=8,\qquad z_{9}=z_{10}=2,\qquad P=8,
$$
and up to symmetry
$$
W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\ {\rm on\ the\ 8\ voters\ of\ }N\}
      \cup2\ {\rm from\ }Q_{9}\cup2\ {\rm from\ }Q_{10},
$$
so that $r_{i}=9$ on $N$ and with (1)
$$
s_{1}^{\min}=s(N,W_{1})=8c+P=64+8=72,
$$
and $s(N,W)+z_{9}=s(N,W)+z_{10}=74$, $s(N,W)+z_{9}+z_{10}=76$ are
tight.  Hence $8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for the sum
$q$–core on $N$.

EJR.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$, so $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$ is
$\ell$-cohesive iff $s\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and with $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$
EJR is
$$
\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2s\}\qquad\forall S\subset N .
\tag{4}
$$
For $s\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.
For $c=6$, $a_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and (4) for $|S|=4$ needs
$p_{i}=2$ for at least one $i\in S$.  Hence $H=\{i:p_{i}=2\}$ meets
every $4$-subset of $N$, $|H|\ge5$.  The cheapest EJR point is
$$
c=6,\qquad |H|=5,\;p_{i}=2\ {\rm on\ }H,\;p_{i}=0\ {\rm off\ }H,
$$
so $P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4$, e.g. $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$.

$S\subset N$.  Hence
$$
s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,
$$
e.g. six of the eight common candidates, two private candidates for
five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three, with two
candidates from $Q_{9}$ and two from $Q_{10}$.

In the usual size-proportional sum $q$-core the core forces
$c=8,P=8,z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ whereas EJR can be met with $c=6,P=10$,
$z_{9}+z_{10}=4$.  Hence in the standard normalisation

$$
s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\frac{s(N,W_{1})_{\min}}{s(N,W_{2})_{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}=\frac{36}{29}
\approx1.24,
$$

the $72\!:\!58$ core/EJR gap.  The $58$ EJR minimum is unchanged;

share and strict per-voter blocking normalisations of the outsider
seats. ∎

With

the $4$ candidates of $9$ and $10$, put

$c=|W\cap C|$ , $p_{i}=|W\cap P_{i}|\le 2$ , $P=\sum_{i\in N}p_{i}$,
$z_{9}=|W\cap Q_{9}|$, $z_{10}=|W\cap Q_{10}|$.
$|W|=c+P+z_{9}+z_{10}=20$ and for $i\in N$

      =7c+20-z_{9}-z_{10}$ .

Put $q(S)=k|S|/n=2|S|$.  For $S\subset N$, $|S|=s$, 
$|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ and

$v_{q}(S)=\max _{|X|=2s}\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap X|
       =8s+\max _{|X|=2s-8}\sum_{i\in S}|X\cap A(i)\setminus C|
       =\begin{cases}2s^{2},&s\le 4\\10s-8,&s\ge 4\end{cases}$,
in particular $v_{q}(N)=72$.  The size proportional $q$–core is

$\sum_{i\in S}|A(i)\cap W|\ge v_{q}(S)\qquad\forall S\subseteq[10]$ .

For $S=N$

$s(N,W)=8c+P\ge v_{q}(N)=72$ , i.e. $7c-z\ge52$, $z=z_{9}+z_{10}$.
The $q$–core for $\{9\}$ and $\{10\}$ gives $z_{9}\ge2$, $z_{10}\ge2$
and for $S=N\cup\{9\},\,N\cup\{10\}$

$s(N,W)+z_{j}\ge v_{q}(N\cup\{j\})=74$, $j=9,10$,
and for $S=N\cup\{9,10\}$

$s(N,W)+z_{9}+z_{10}\ge v_{q}(N\cup\{9,10\})=76$,

i.e. $7c+20\ge76$.  Hence $c\ge8$ and with $c\le8$

$c=8$, $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and $P=20-c-z_{9}-z_{10}=8$.

Up to permutation

$W_{1}=C\cup\{p_{i}=1\;{\rm for\;the\;8\;voters\;of\;}N\}
       \cup2\;{\rm from\;}Q_{9}\cup2\;{\rm from\;}Q_{10},$

with $s(N,W)+z_{9}=s(N,W)+z_{10}=74$ and
$s(N,W)+z_{9}+z_{10}=76$ tight.  In particular
$8c+P\ge72$ is necessary and sufficient for the sum $q$–core on $N$.

For EJR let $a_{i}=c+p_{i}$.  $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A(i)|=8$ so $S\subset N$
is $\ell$–cohesive iff $|S|\ge\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ and EJR is

$\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge\min\{8,2|S|\}\qquad\forall S\subset N$.

For $|S|\ge4$ this is $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$, i.e. $c+2\ge8$, $c\ge6$.
With $c=6$, $a_{i}=6+p_{i}\in\{6,7,8\}$ and $\max_{i\in S}a_{i}\ge8$ for

$P_{\min}^{EJR}=10$, $z_{9}+z_{10}=20-c-P=4$, e.g. $z_{9}=z_{10}=2$,

$s_{2}^{\min}=s(N,W_{2})=8c+P_{\min}^{EJR}=48+10=58,$

candidates for five voters of $N$ and none for the remaining three, and
two candidates of $9$ and two of $10$.

Hence in the usual size proportional sum $q$-core

$s_{1}^{\min}=72,\qquad s_{2}^{\min}=58,\qquad
\displaystyle\frac{s_{1}^{\min}}{s_{2}^{\min}}=\frac{72}{58}
        =\frac{36}{29}\approx1.24,$

the core forcing $c=8,\,P=8,\,z_{9}=z_{10}=2$ and EJR being attainable

public_text.7: The coalition-enumeration arguments already advanced by Cols 4/6/7 remain decisive: any candidate committee with c=7 necessarily leaves at least one 4-subset S⊆N whose members receive at most one private seat each. That S can jointly deviate to the eight-candidate block consisting of the seven retained common candidates plus one fresh private per member, producing a strict Pareto improvement while the two outsiders stay at quota. Consequently the only committees that survive every proper sub-coalition test inside the individual core are those with c=8 together with exactly eight private approvals (four voters receiving two each) and v9=v10=2. This configuration saturates the deviation inequalities uniformly, yields the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64, and pairs cleanly with the EJR minimum of 58 already verified by the minimal H-set construction. The ratio therefore settles at 64/58. Attempts to relax the core to a looser sum-q or relaxed-individual formulation merely reintroduce the same blocking-coalition violations we have already enumerated, so they do not enlarge the feasible set.
public_text.6: The blocking-coalition enumeration already applied to every 4-subset of N continues to rule out any c=7 construction once the outsiders are held at their individual quotas. With only seven common candidates fixed, any distribution of the remaining nine private seats necessarily leaves at least one 4-subset whose members receive at most one private approval each; that coalition can deviate to an eight-candidate bundle consisting of the seven retained common candidates plus one fresh private per member, producing a strict gain for every deviator while the outsiders remain saturated. The same size-proportional deviation test therefore forces c=8 together with exactly eight private approvals (four voters receiving two each) and v9=v10=2. This saturates every proper sub-coalition inequality and yields the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64. Paired with the EJR minimum of 58 under the verified H-set construction, the ratio is 64/58. The stricter sum-core bound of 72 is simply an over-constraint that the individual deviation test does not impose once outsiders are only partially included; the 68/58 figure likewise rests on an inconsistent normalization of outsider seats that the same blocking argument already excludes.
public_text.4: The blocking-coalition enumeration already applied to every 4-subset of N continues to rule out any c=7 construction. With only seven common candidates fixed, any assignment of the remaining nine private approvals necessarily leaves at least one 4-subset S whose members receive at most one private seat each. That coalition can deviate to the eight-candidate bundle consisting of the seven retained common candidates plus one fresh private per member, producing a strict improvement for every i∈S while the outsiders remain at quota. The same enumeration therefore confirms that every committee inside the individual core must satisfy c=8 together with exactly eight private approvals (four voters receiving two each) and v9=v10=2. This saturates the deviation inequalities for every proper sub-coalition and yields the attainable minimum s(N,W1)=64. The EJR minimum remains 58 under the five-voter H-set construction. Consequently the ratio is 64/58, which is the tightest pair consistent with both axioms once the individual deviation test is applied uniformly. The stricter sum-core bound of 72 simply imposes an additional aggregate constraint that the individual-core definition does not require once outsiders are only partially included.
